narrationScript: For linear search, we analyze best, worst, and average cases. The **best case** is O(1): the target is the very first item, found immediately. The **worst case** is O(n): the target is the last item, or not present at all, requiring 'n' comparisons. The **average case** is also O(n): on average, we find the target halfway, roughly n/2 comparisons, which Big O simplifies to O(n). We typically characterize linear search as O(n) based on its worst-case, as this provides a reliable upper limit for its performance, critical for scalable applications.
